problems.reason: The arrow only applies at depth 4, so stability-from-pole-locations@3, which iir-filters@3 relies on, has no prerequisites at all; it should be stability-from-pole-locations@3 needs z-transform-region-of-convergence@3 (and through it poles and zeros).
The pole-location test rests on h being absolutely summable even at the apply level, so this arrow should start at stability-from-pole-locations@3, not @4.

You can't estimate a response from distances to poles and zeros without knowing them, but at depth 3 nothing reaches poles-and-zeros (transfer-function@3 doesn't need it); the arrow should be @3 needs poles-and-zeros@3.
Knowing that a signal is a function of t doesn't depend on graph shifting or flipping; signal-time-operations already carries that prerequisite, so this arrow should be dropped.
Poles and zeros are just the roots of the numerator and denominator; partial fractions uses those roots rather than being needed to understand them, so this arrow should be dropped.

The convolution theorem is stated for the continuous-time Fourier transform and uses the convolution integral, but it only reaches discrete-time convolution, and continuous-time-convolution feeds nothing; add convolution-theorem@3 needs continuous-time-convolution@3.

The capstone includes the FIR-or-IIR choice, but windowing is the only design method in the map; add an IIR design method such as 'IIR low-pass design by pole-zero placement (e.g. a first-order recursive low-pass)' so the IIR choice can be carried out.
